chunks: Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamadani (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated, saying: 'Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abu Umayr, from Ibrahim ibn Ziyad al-Karkhi, from Abu Abdillah, from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Whoever dies without ascribing a partner to Allah, whether he did good or evil, will enter Paradise.

key_terms.وَلَا يُشْرِكُ بِاللَّهِ شَيْئًا: without ascribing a partner to Allah

ai.seo_question: Does a Muslim who committed sins enter Paradise if they did not commit Shirk?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq cites this chain to affirm the principle of *al-ghalabah* (dominance) of faith over sin, a key tenet in Shia theology distinguishing it from the Mu'tazilite view that major sins exclude one from Paradise entirely. The hadith clarifies that while sins incur punishment, they do not sever the bond of *Tawhid*, ensuring eventual entry for those who die with pure monotheism. This supports the Shia doctrine of *al-Wa'd wa al-Wa'id* (Promise and Threat), where divine mercy ultimately prevails for monotheists.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 5. Ahmed ibn Ziyad ibn Ja’far al-Hamadani (ra) said, that `Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, on the authority of his father, from Muhammad ibn Abu `Umayr, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Ziyad al-Karkhi from Abu `Abdillah, from his father, from his grandfather (AS), that The Messenger of Allah (sw) said: “
Whoever dies without ascribing a partner to Allah, will enter Heaven regardless of whether he has done good or evil.”
